name: Sterling-Nakamura Personal Atmospheric Filter PAF-4
description: A compact rebreather mask that filters atmospheric contaminants, toxins, biological agents, and particulates while remaining small enough to be worn inconspicuously in urban environments. The PAF-4 covers nose and mouth with a low-profile mesh filter that uses activated charcoal, HEPA filtration, and a catalytic conversion layer that neutralizes chemical agents. The mask is powered by a micro-fan that maintains positive pressure inside the filter zone, preventing unfiltered air from entering through seal gaps. Sterling-Nakamura issues them to personnel operating in GLMZ's contaminated lower-tier districts.
story_hooks: PAF-4 masks have been distributed free in a Tier 1 district as a humanitarian gesture — but the masks contain a micro-transmitter that tracks the wearer's breathing patterns and location.
A contamination event has overwhelmed PAF-4 filter capacity — the masks are providing false confidence while slowly allowing toxins through, and wearers think they are safe when they are not.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting rebreather mask that hugs the lower face like a second skin. The design prioritizes discretion over bulk, with clean lines and minimal protrusion. The mesh filter panel dominates the front, creating a semi-transparent window that reveals layered filtration cartridges beneath. Subtle ribbing along the sides suggests reinforced flex-points for comfort during extended wear.
physical_description.dimensions: Approximately 12 cm wide × 8 cm tall × 4 cm deep at the deepest point. Fits entirely below the cheekbones, leaving eyes and forehead exposed.
physical_description.weight_description: 120 grams total—light enough for all-day wear without fatigue. Handheld when not worn; negligible burden when mounted on face.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite with embedded micro-fan housing. Charcoal and HEPA cartridge chambers molded into the structure.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal-gray housing with a brushed titanium accent strip running horizontally across the filter mesh. The mesh itself has a faint iridescence—signature of catalytic conversion coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary body with matt-black mesh panel and silver-gray accent stripping. Subtle cyan indicator lights embedded at the corners where the mask contacts the jawline.
physical_description.interface_elements: Two discrete circular LED indicators (cyan and amber) at jaw-level corners show battery/filter status. A minimalist power button recessed into the right temple area. Magnetic cartridge release points visible on either side of the mesh panel. No screen display—status communicated through light color and pulse rate.
distinctive_features: Layered mesh panel revealing stacked filter cartridges—a transparent view of the filtration architecture
Faint cyan glow from catalytic conversion layer visible through mesh under certain angles
Micro-perforations along the cheekbone contact points for micro-ventilation and comfort
Sterling-Nakamura embossed logo on the right temple in chrome-finish lettering
Magnetic quick-release cartridge system—dual silver snap-points where filters engage
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura logo (stylized 'SN' interlocked design) in chrome relief on right temple. Tiny regulatory stamp (GLMZ-TIER1-CERTIFIED) etched below logo. Cartridge compatibility marking on filter housing.
physical_description.condition_typical: In daily use, light condensation may bead on the mesh from exhaled breath due to positive pressure. The cyan status lights pulse softly when battery is above 75%; they remain solid when dropping below that threshold. After extended use in heavily contaminated zones, the mesh takes on a visible gray-brown patina—visual indicator that cartridge replacement is due.
